pump-house-cutaway.title: The Byrd Park Pump House: Cutaway
pump-house-cutaway.notes: research done: feasibility 3.5 of 5; rough draft, then d1-d3 on 2026-11-18 on The American Engineer pp. 260-261 (HathiTrust full scans). Approved: d3, the pumped-water variant; d2 kept as cutaways/pump-house-1885.json. Known faults for rc1 (owner: list, not pre-accepted): gang positions along the room inferred; tailraces' size and line inferred; penstocks square in section; south walkway a large blank plane in the cut; sections print small (about 8-9 in each at 32 x 24); context map uses today's OSM river and canal lines, with one gap closed; west wing's end-wall lancets show as slivers; the pumped line crosses the forebay wall schematically (the suction's intake was at the west end). Plate BPPH-01, set BPPH (2026-11-18). rc1 inspected once; fix round -> rc2 (f67df4e).

Before publication: an independent fact check (154 claims) and three independent reads with Claude (scholar, dignity and harm, first-time reader), all fixes applied; outlines redrawn from the public-domain scan; the highway finding stated with its base rate (D 30% of graded land, 65% of the highway inside it, about 56% expected from location alone). holc-richmond-transcription.title: Our own transcription of Richmond's 48 HOLC area-description forms, from the public-domain scans
holc-richmond-transcription.decision: Follow-up, after the redlining and Jackson Ward stories are out (owner, 2026-11-22). A second independent keying of all 48 forms, compared field by field with the first reading on branch holc-audit (tools/holc/audit/); disagreements read a third time. Adds the typed area headings and the informant names. Published as open data with scan page and field for each value. Not started. The audit found 27 value differences from the lab's transcription, read once; no outreach to the lab unless the owner chooses (draft in outputs/stories/redlining/audit/note-to-the-lab.md). A national pilot (about 80 forms, 10 cities) is a separate project, not planned.

jackson-ward-navy-hill-streets.title: Trace the 1952 streets of Navy Hill and Gilpin Court for the Jackson Ward views
jackson-ward-navy-hill-streets.decision: Follow-up (owner, 2026-11-23). In the story's 1925 and 1952 views several of today's streets run through houses the 1952 Sanborn sheets print: the curved approach to the 5th Street bridge, Maggie L. Walker Place, East Leigh and East Jackson Streets, alleys, possibly Hill Street. An era rule cannot remove them without leaving gaps, because the 1952 streets there were never read off the sheets. Also check the lost-north-5th-street join, which may draw 5th Street on two lines, and the unverified 1992 date on the old Chamberlayne bridge (BridgeLookup 583420). Found by the pocket guide work; see outputs/stories/jackson-ward/fix-1952-bridges/fix.md. Not started.

series-richmond-downtown-time-rebuild.title: Rebuild the whole Downtown Richmond through time series once, so every pair of years compares like with like
series-richmond-downtown-time-rebuild.decision: Backlog (owner, 2026-11-23). The 26 years on the series page mix builds from November 14 (14 years) and November 16-17 (12 years), which draw the canal and basin, the Free Bridge and the frame height differently, so some pairs show changes in method beside the history (1860 against 1865 looks like this; not confirmed). One run of the series on the Mac, where the cached data is, then look at the pairs on the page's jump list. Also fixes the 1870 caption, which says Shockoe Creek runs open until 1877 where the history file now has 1890. Released editions (Richmond 1925, 1950 and others on sale) are frozen: the rebuild is for the explorer, and any sold year keeps its released build as the print's record.

series-richmond-floods.title: Richmond's floods over time: how much went under, before and after the floodwall
series-richmond-floods.decision: Worth pursuing (owner, 2026-11-23 20:03), on Opus 5.5 subagents; no outside parties to be contacted, public sources only. Decided: each flood on the city of its own year; 1x terrain; Gaston as depths at named places with a soft pool and the gates open; one neutral sentence on the 2009 lawsuit; a radar rain map for the Shockoe valley; 1771 as a labeled estimate; an Agnes-against-today's-wall plate. Drawing levels (ft NAVD88 at the City Locks): 1771 38.0, Agnes 35.5, 1985 29.7, Camille 27.6, 1936 26.5, Fran 22.7, 2020 17.0. Unknown and staying so: the wall's top elevation and its openings' sills. In work: drawing d1 on branch feature/flood-surface; the rain map. Next gate: the owner approves the look. Record: drafts/richmond-floods/casestudy/.
